faq.more: Something else? Visit the <help>help center</help> or <contact>contact us</contact>.
faq.q1: What exactly do I get from one campaign?
faq.a1: {pieces} pieces built around one idea: 1 YouTube script, 5 short-form video scripts, 3 LinkedIn posts, 4 X posts and threads, 2 carousels, 3 Instagram story sequences and 2 newsletters, plus an SEO keyword strategy for the whole campaign.
faq.q2: Does ContentArc publish to my social accounts?
faq.a2: Yes, on paid plans. Connect your accounts once, create a content plan for a campaign, and ContentArc publishes the posts you approve to LinkedIn, X, Facebook, Instagram, Threads, Bluesky, Pinterest, TikTok and YouTube at the best times for your audience: posts, carousels and stories designed with your brand kit and AI illustrations, and videos made from your scripts (AI voice-over, stock footage, subtitles). You see a preview of each post exactly as it will appear, and nothing goes out without your approval. Newsletters are planned on your calendar for you to send; you can also copy or export any piece.
faq.a3: Yes. The free plan includes 1 campaign a month and 1 product, with no credit card required. Upgrade whenever you need more.
faq.a4: ContentArc uses leading large language models (including Anthropic Claude) and asks them for structured, platform-native output that is checked before it reaches you.
faq.a5: You do. Everything you create in ContentArc is yours to publish, edit and reuse. As with any AI-assisted writing, review each piece before publishing. See our <terms>terms</terms>.
faq.a6: English, French, German, Italian, Spanish, Portuguese, Chinese, Russian, Korean and Arabic, for both the app and the content it writes.
faq.a7: A short call-to-action like “Comment GUIDE and I'll DM you the link”. Pair it with a DM automation tool to turn comments into leads for your offer.
faq.a8: Yes. Manage or cancel your subscription from the billing portal in the app; your campaigns stay in your account.
faq.a9: We only use your data to run the service. Read the <privacy>privacy policy</privacy> for details on providers and retention.
faq.q10: Can ContentArc make a demo video of my app?
faq.a10: Yes, on Publisher and Enterprise. Give the address of your web app, or upload your Android app (.apk) or an iPhone simulator build, with a test account. ContentArc looks at your app and proposes a storyboard that you edit and approve. It then performs the steps in the real app and turns them into a voiced walkthrough and short vertical clips. The sign-in is never shown in the video.
faq.a11: Paid plans see each published post's views, likes, comments, shares and link clicks, by network and over time. Publisher and Enterprise also compare marketing angles, formats and weekdays, so you can see whether Problem-Agitate-Solve or Build in Public works better for your product. Figures come from each network, and some networks report more than others.
faq.q12: How does the niche and competitor watch work?
faq.a12: Describe your niche and add the competitors you want to follow. Every week ContentArc researches what's getting attention there and summarises the hooks, formats and topics that work, with links to its sources. It never copies anyone's posts: you choose which findings inspire your next campaign.
faq.a13: Yes, on Publisher and Enterprise. Create API keys in the app to start campaigns and read posts and analytics from Zapier, Make or your own code, and add webhooks to be told when a campaign is ready or when a post is published or fails.

help.title: Help center
help.intro: Everything you need to go from one idea to a published campaign.

blocks.x: Getting started

x: [Sign in]({signUpUrl}) with your email. We send you a one-time sign-in link, so there's no password to remember.
Open **Brand Brain** and add the product or brand you want to promote.
Click **New campaign**, write one idea, pick an angle and generate.
Review the {pieces} pieces, refine what you like, then create a content plan and approve the posts to publish (or export them).

blocks.x: Brand Brain
The Brand Brain stores what you sell so every campaign speaks to the right people and points to the right place. For each entry you set:

x: **Type**: ebook, SaaS, digital product, brand, specific offer or other.
**Target audience**: who it's for and the problem they feel right now.
**Value proposition**: the concrete outcome you deliver.
**Lead magnet / CTA link**: where your content sends people.

blocks.x: Write a first draft of the audience and value proposition, then click **Improve with AI**. ContentArc sharpens your wording without inventing facts, and you can undo it if you prefer your version.
Creating a campaign
Choose a product, describe one idea (a chapter, a feature launch, a lesson learned, a video concept) and pick one of four angles:

x: **Problem · Agitate · Solve**: name the pain, raise the stakes, present the fix.
**AIDA**: attention, interest, desire, action.
**Contrarian**: challenge a common belief in your niche.
**Build in public**: share the real numbers, process and lessons.

blocks.x: Generation usually takes one to three minutes. You get an SEO keyword strategy plus {pieces} pieces: 1 YouTube script, 5 short-video scripts, 3 LinkedIn posts, 4 X posts and threads, 2 carousels, 3 story sequences and 2 newsletters.
From idea to published posts, step by step
A new campaign shows a **Next steps** checklist at the top. Each step ticks itself as you go:

x: **Review and polish** the {pieces} pieces in the format tabs. Edit anything, use the **Copilot**, mark good pieces **Ready**. Carousels, stories, videos and newsletters are **scripts**: their text says what to show, and your followers see the designed result, never the instructions.
**Connect your social accounts** once per brand in **Social accounts** (paid plans): LinkedIn, X, Facebook, Instagram, Threads, Bluesky and Pinterest.

**Create the content plan** (7, 14 or 28 days). ContentArc dates every piece in a strategic order at good times for each network, in your **audience's time zone** (worked out from your Brand Brain, or chosen by you). Adjust the posting times per channel, click any date to move a single post, and use **Fix automatically** when two posts would compete on the same network.

**Prepare the visuals**: carousels and stories are designed automatically in your brand style, with an AI illustration on each slide. In the slide editor, edit any slide and click **Create image** to draw its picture from its description or its text, or upload your own images. Add an AI image or your own photo for Instagram and Pinterest posts.

**Approve and schedule**: check the **Preview as published** (the exact text and images each network receives), then approve one post at a time, or **Approve & schedule all** in the plan. Nothing is published before you approve; you can turn on automatic approval when you create the plan.
**Track in the Calendar**: move posts by drag and drop, open the live links, and reschedule anything that failed (you also get an email).
Videos and newsletters stay on your calendar as reminders: record or send them yourself, or **Export** the campaign.

blocks.x: **Take a tour** any time from the **?** menu at the top of the app, or from the checklist. Small **ⓘ** icons next to each section explain what it does.
Editing & the AI Copilot

Every piece is editable in place and saves automatically. Use the status switch to track **Draft → Ready → Published**. The **Copilot** menu rewrites a piece to be punchier, shorter, longer, more story-driven or stronger on the call-to-action, or follows your own instruction. Each rewrite can be undone.
Publishing & export

On paid plans, ContentArc publishes for you. Connect each brand's accounts once in **Social accounts**. On a campaign, create a **content plan**: ContentArc dates every piece at good times for each network in your audience's time zone and flags overlaps. Add an AI image (or your own) where needed, check each post's preview, then **approve & schedule** posts, or turn on automatic approval. Follow and move everything in the **Calendar**; you get an email if a post fails. Videos and newsletters are planned for you to post yourself. You can also copy a piece with one click, copy its DM automation hook, or use **Export** to download:

x: a **.zip of Markdown files**, one file per piece;
a **single Markdown file** with the whole campaign;
a **CSV** you can import into bulk schedulers.

blocks.x: **Carousels and stories**: set your colours, font, logo and handle once in the **brand kit** (Brand Brain). ContentArc turns the script into slides, adds an AI illustration to each slide and renders them in your brand style; you can edit any slide, create a new image for it, or upload your own images. Carousels go to Instagram, Facebook, Threads and X, and to LinkedIn as a swipeable PDF; story frames are published one by one.
Analytics & link clicks

Open **Analytics** to see how your published posts perform. ContentArc reads each post's counters from the network it went out on for 30 days (every hour at first, then less often): views or impressions, likes, comments, shares, saves and clicks. Paid plans see totals, a breakdown by network and the top posts; Publisher and Enterprise also see results **by marketing angle, by format and by weekday**.
Facebook, Instagram and Threads accounts connected before analytics existed may need to be reconnected in **Social accounts** to share reach and clicks.

**Link click tracking**: in Brand Brain, edit a product and turn on **Count link clicks**. When a post is published, its link is replaced by a short ContentArc link that counts clicks per post and per network (the previews networks make of a link are not counted), then sends people to your page with its UTM tags. Leave it off to keep your own domain in your posts; the UTM tags still show up in your own analytics.
History & recycling

**History** lists every published post with its results, across campaigns and brands. Search it, filter by product or network, and click **Recycle this post** on a post that worked: ContentArc rewrites it with another marketing angle (for example from AIDA to Contrarian) as a new draft in the same campaign, ready to plan again. Recycling a post counts as one AI Copilot rewrite. New campaigns also take your published posts into account, so they don't repeat what you already said.
Niche & competitor watch

Open **Insights**, describe your niche and add the competitors you want to follow (by website or handle). Every week ContentArc researches the web and writes a short report: the topics, hooks and formats getting attention, each finding with a link to its source. Findings without a source are left out. You can also refresh a report on demand, within your plan's monthly reports.
When you create a campaign, choose a report as inspiration: its findings guide the angle and the hooks, without copying anyone's posts.
SaaS demo videos
On Publisher and Enterprise, ContentArc can record your product. On the **New campaign** page, click **SaaS demo video** (your product must be of type SaaS in Brand Brain):

x: **Choose the app**: your **web app** (its address, and its sign-in page if it has one), your **Android app** (upload the .apk) or your **iPhone app** (a simulator build: the .app folder from Xcode, zipped; App Store files can't be used).
**Add a test account** if the app needs a sign-in. It is stored encrypted, typed only into the sign-in screen and never appears in the video. Never use a real customer's account.
**Choose what to show**: a tour of the product, getting started, or one feature you describe.
**Review the storyboard**: ContentArc looks at your app and proposes scenes, each with the steps to perform, the narration and an on-screen caption. Edit or remove anything, then approve.

**Get your videos**: the steps are performed in the real app, in a cloud browser or on a hosted phone, with a voice-over and captions. You get a walkthrough for YouTube and up to four short vertical clips, saved as drafts in the campaign so you can schedule them like any other post.

blocks.x: If a button can't be found by its label, ContentArc looks at the screen to find it. A step that still can't be done is skipped, and the demo page tells you why.
API & webhooks

On Publisher and Enterprise, open **Developers** from the account menu to create API keys and webhooks. With a key, your tools can start a campaign (from an idea or an article's address), follow its progress and read posts and analytics. Webhooks tell your tools when a campaign is ready and when a post is published or fails; every delivery is signed so you can check it comes from ContentArc. The full reference is in the app.
Plans & billing

Compare plans in the [pricing section](/#pricing). Upgrade from **Plans** inside the app; payments are handled securely by Stripe. Change plan, update your card, download invoices or cancel from **Billing**. A cancelled plan stays active until the end of the period you paid for.
Account & languages

Switch the interface language from the flag menu in the top bar; new campaigns default to that language, and you can pick a different one per campaign. Light, dark and system themes are in the same bar. Manage email preferences in **Settings**.
Sign-in problems

x: Check your spam or promotions folder for the sign-in email.
Each link works once and expires after about an hour. Request a new one if needed.
Requesting a new link cancels the previous one, so use the most recent email.

privacy.x: This policy explains how {company} (“ContentArc”, “we”) handles personal data when you use {site} and the ContentArc app at {app}. We are the controller of this data.
Data we collect

x: **Account data**: email address, name (optional), preferred language, sign-in history.

**Content you provide**: products and brands in your Brand Brain (including your brand kit and logo), campaign ideas, the content generated and edited in the app, and the images created or uploaded for your posts.
**Usage data**: counts of campaigns and AI rewrites (to apply plan limits).
**Billing data**: plan, subscription status and a Stripe customer reference. Card details are collected and stored by Stripe, never by us.
**Email preferences**: whether you opted in to marketing emails, and when.
**Contact form**: your name, email and message when you write to us.
**Technical data**: IP address and request logs kept by our hosting provider for security.

**Connected social accounts**: the name, handle and profile picture of each account you connect, the posts you schedule, their images and their publishing results. Access to your social accounts is held by our publishing provider (Upload-Post), not by us.
**Performance data**: the counters each network reports for your published posts (such as views, likes, comments, shares and clicks).
**Link clicks**: if you turn on click tracking, the number of clicks on each short link and the time of the latest click. We don't store who clicked.
**Niche and competitor watch**: your niche description, the competitors you choose to follow (names, websites or public handles) and the reports written from public web pages.
**SaaS demo videos**: your app's address or the app build you upload, the test account you provide (stored encrypted), the storyboard, and the screenshots, recordings and videos made of your app.
**API and webhooks**: a fingerprint of each API key (never the key itself), your webhook addresses and a log of their deliveries.

privacy.x: How we use it

x: To provide the service: authenticate you, store your work and generate campaigns (contract).
To process payments and manage subscriptions (contract, legal obligations).
To send service emails such as sign-in links, welcome and billing messages (contract).
To send product updates and tips, only if you opted in (consent, withdrawable anytime).
To keep the service secure and prevent abuse (legitimate interest).
To answer your messages (legitimate interest).

privacy.x: We do not sell your personal data and we do not use your content to train AI models.
Service providers
We share data only with providers that process it on our behalf to run ContentArc:

x: **Supabase**: database, authentication and file storage.
**Cloudflare**: website and application hosting, security and spam protection for forms.
**Stripe**: payments and subscription billing.
**Brevo**: transactional email, contact management and (if you opted in) newsletters.

**AI model providers** (such as Anthropic, OpenAI, Google or DeepSeek): your product details and campaign ideas are sent to the model that generates or rewrites your content. We use their business APIs; how each provider handles API data is set out in its own terms.
**Upload-Post**: publishes the posts you approve to the social accounts you connect, and holds the access you grant to those accounts.

**Image model providers** (such as Black Forest Labs, Ideogram, OpenAI, Google or Cloudflare Workers AI): a text description of the image, written from your post or slide, is sent to generate post and slide images.

**Stock photo providers** (such as Pexels, Pixabay or Unsplash): when you choose stock photos, a few search words written from your post or slide are sent to find matching photos. No personal data is sent.

**Other publishing routes**: depending on how you connect an account, posts go out directly through the network's own API (Meta for Facebook and Instagram, Threads, Bluesky) or through Zernio or Buffer, which then hold the access you grant.
**Browserless**: runs the cloud browser that opens your web app to record SaaS demo videos.
**Appetize**: runs the hosted Android and iPhone devices for mobile demo videos, using the app build you upload.
**Shotstack**: assembles videos from scripts, screenshots and recordings. Voice-overs are generated by an AI text-to-speech provider (such as OpenAI).

**Web research**: the niche and competitor watch uses an AI model provider's web search (such as Anthropic's). It receives your niche description and the competitors you follow, not your account data.

privacy.x: Some providers process data outside the UK and the European Economic Area, including in the United States. Where required, transfers rely on appropriate safeguards such as the UK International Data Transfer Addendum and the European Commission's standard contractual clauses.
Cookies and local storage

The app uses strictly necessary cookies to keep you signed in and remember your language and time zone (so dates and posting times are shown in your local time), and your browser's local storage to remember your theme and unsaved drafts. This website uses a language cookie and local storage for your theme; it does not use advertising or tracking cookies.
Retention

We keep your account and content while your account is active. You can ask us to delete your account at any time by email; we then delete your personal data within 30 days, except records we must keep for legal or accounting reasons (such as invoices). Contact-form messages are kept for up to 24 months.
Your rights

Depending on where you live (including under the UK GDPR and the EU GDPR), you can access, correct, export or delete your data, object to or restrict certain processing, and withdraw consent at any time. Unsubscribe from marketing emails with the link in any email or in the app's Settings. To exercise your rights, email [{email}](mailto:{email}). You may also complain to a data protection authority: in the UK, the Information Commissioner's Office (ico.org.uk), or the authority in your EU country of residence.
Security
Data is encrypted in transit, access is restricted with row-level security, and secrets are held server-side only. No system is perfectly secure, but we work to protect your information.
Children
ContentArc is not intended for anyone under 16, and we do not knowingly collect their data.
Changes
We'll update this page when our practices change and notify you of significant changes by email or in the app.
Contact
Questions about privacy? Write to [{email}](mailto:{email}) or use our [contact form](/contact). You can also reach {company} at [{companyEmail}](mailto:{companyEmail}) or by post at {address}.

terms.x: These terms form an agreement between you and {company}, a company registered in {jurisdiction} (company number {number}), registered office {address} (“ContentArc”, “we”), for the use of ContentArc, including {site} and the app at {app}. By creating an account or using the service, you accept them.
1. The service

ContentArc helps you plan, write and publish marketing content with AI: it generates multi-channel campaigns from your product information and ideas, lets you edit them, organises them in a content plan and calendar, creates images for them and, on paid plans, publishes the posts you approve to the social accounts you connect. You can also export your content.

When you connect social accounts, you authorise us and our publishing provider (Upload-Post) to publish, on your behalf and at the times you set, the posts you approve (or that you choose to approve automatically for a campaign). You can disconnect accounts or unschedule posts at any time. You are responsible for the content you publish and for complying with each network's rules. Social networks can change, limit or withdraw access at any time, so we cannot guarantee that a post will be published, published on time or stay online; if a post fails, we will tell you by email.

ContentArc also measures how your published posts perform, researches your niche and the competitors you choose using public web pages and, on the plans that include them, records demo videos of your app and offers an API and webhooks. Research reports summarise public information with links to their sources and may be incomplete; treat them as inspiration, not as guaranteed facts.

**SaaS demo videos.** By starting a demo, you confirm that you own the app or are authorised to use it this way, that the account you provide is a test account, and that you authorise us and our providers (Browserless for the cloud browser, Appetize for hosted phones) to open or install the app, sign in and perform the steps you approve. Don't record screens that show other people's personal data. You are responsible for what the video shows.

**API.** Keep your API keys secret: anyone with a key can act on your account within your plan. We may limit the number of requests and suspend keys that are abused. Webhooks are delivered on a best-effort basis, with retries.
2. Your account

You must be at least 16 and provide an email address you control. You are responsible for activity on your account and for keeping access to your email secure. Tell us promptly about any unauthorized use.
3. Plans, payment and cancellation

x: The free plan is offered with the limits shown on our pricing page and may change over time.
Paid plans are billed in advance, monthly or yearly, through Stripe, and renew automatically until cancelled.

You can cancel anytime from the billing portal; your plan stays active until the end of the current period. Payments are non-refundable, except as described in section 4 (right of withdrawal) or where required by law.
